lines: d12: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Jack Hicks is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d12: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d12: 🕯️ Jack Hicks is dead — a stranger. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d12: What Jack kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d12: "Jack's gone." Daniyar looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Jack." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d12: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Brian blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d12: 📖 LEARNED: Animal Behavior (Level 1). Most animals flee. Give them an escape route and they take it. Cornered animals fight.
d12: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d12: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Jack Hicks, 12 days. The mantle passes to Brian Otieno.
d12: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Brian Otieno, 31 — a zookeeper. His hands know different work now: Beast-calm.
d12: The village's quarrel was with Jack — and Jack is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d12: At the grave, Nathan, Soo, Daria and 2 more speak for Brian — "Jack trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d12: The fire knew Brian before the Codex did — his name already carried weight here.
d58: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Brian Otieno is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d58: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
